title: Best Buy $15 minimum wage kicks in for tens of thousands of hourly workers
summary: Best Buy implemented a new $15 minimum wage for its hourly employees in the U.S. beginning August 2, 2020. This represents a 4% pay increase for many workers and follows a period of appreciation pay during the COVID-19 pandemic. The decision comes as Best Buy experienced significant growth in online sales and overall retail sales during the pandemic.

title: Goldman Sachs Buys Into E-Commerce Warehouse Play with Dalfen Industrial
summary: Goldman Sachs Group's merchant banking division has partnered with Dalfen Industrial of Dallas to invest in a $500 million portfolio of 46 last-mile distribution buildings, totaling 6.3 million square feet. These properties are strategically located in major population centers and key logistics corridors, catering to e-commerce tenants with high occupancy rates. The investment highlights the increasing importance of last-mile distribution centers, especially with the surge in e-commerce driven by COVID-19.

title: Better Buy: Cisco Systems vs. Oracle
summary: This article compares Cisco Systems (CSCO) and Oracle (ORCL), two tech giants that have had to adapt to the advent of cloud computing. It analyzes how each company is navigating the shift to cloud-based solutions and the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on their businesses. The author concludes that Cisco is the better investment due to its transformation to a SaaS model, strong position in networking, diversified products, and higher dividend yield.

title: Online payment platform partners with AWS for cloud transformation
summary: Global Payments Inc. is collaborating with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to transform its core issuing platform into a secure, cloud-based solution. This multi-year agreement will allow Global Payments to deliver online payment technologies globally, relying on AWS as its preferred cloud provider. The partnership aims to expand the customer base for issuer processing services and explore additional payment product collaborations.

title: Google buys $450M stake in ADT to give Nest a new perch
summary: Google is investing $450 million for a nearly 7% stake in ADT Inc., aiming to expand the reach of its Nest cameras and voice assistant. As part of this partnership, ADT will integrate Nest's internet-connected cameras and Nest Home Hub into its security systems. This deal allows Google to further develop its home management product line and benefit from ADT's extensive customer base.

title: Rainbow Rangers Toys From Mattel’s Fisher-Price Debuts at Walmart Stores Nationwide, Walmart.com and Amazon
summary: Genius Brands International announced the debut of the first 'Rainbow Rangers' toys from Mattel's Fisher-Price, now available at Walmart stores, Walmart.com, and Amazon. The toys feature characters from the hit preschool series, with a comprehensive advertising campaign supporting the launch. Genius Brands is also offering limited-edition lithographs and Certificates of Authenticity to early buyers to celebrate the launch.

title: 'Vital' food brand hatches into Austin's newest publicly traded company
summary: Vital Farms, an Austin-based company known for its pasture-raised eggs and butter, successfully completed its initial public offering (IPO), raising $204.6 million. The company's stock debuted on the Nasdaq Stock Market at $22 per share, solidifying its position as a publicly traded entity focused on ethically produced food. Founded in 2007, Vital Farms holds a significant share of the U.S. retail market for pasture-raised eggs and partners with approximately 200 family farms.

title: As pandemic stretches on, retail bankruptcies approach highest number in a decade
summary: Retail bankruptcies in 2020 are on track to be the highest in a decade, with 43 filings so far this year, surpassing the total for the past eight years. Companies like Le Tote (owner of Lord & Taylor) and Tailored Brands (parent of Men's Wearhouse) are among the latest to file due to the pandemic compounding pre-existing financial challenges. The article details several major retail bankruptcies of 2020 and highlights that more filings are expected as the pandemic continues to impact consumer spending and store operations.

title: Tim Cook Says These 3 Words Guide Every Decision at Apple
summary: Tim Cook stated that "privacy, security, and quality" guide every decision at Apple, especially in its app review process. The article argues that these three words differentiate Apple from its competitors, particularly concerning data privacy and product experience. It emphasizes that these principles provide clarity for Apple's decisions and are foundational to its operations, serving as a lesson for other leaders.

title: Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada Look Favorable Ahead of Earnings
summary: Ahead of earnings season, Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada are showing favorable signals, despite overall S&P 500 profit declines and a historic U.S. GDP plunge in Q2 2020 due to COVID-19. Ivanhoe Mines has seen its shares explode over 142% since mid-March, benefiting from rising metal prices and its strategic location in the DRC, while Franco-Nevada, a gold royalty company, has delivered strong performance and reached number eight on the IBD 50 Stock List. The article highlights strong performances from certain tech and metal mining companies during this period, with gold also reaching near all-time highs.

title: Global Payments Joins Forces with AWS to Deliver the Future of Payments
summary: Global Payments Inc. and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have announced a multi-year collaboration to provide a cloud-based issuer processing platform to financial institutions worldwide. Global Payments will leverage AWS as its preferred cloud provider for issuer processing, utilizing AWS services for scalability, compliance, and enhanced customer experiences. This partnership aims to expand Global Payments' customer base, accelerate innovation in payments technology, and address new global markets.

title: Rodney McMullen, Chairman and CEO of The Kroger Company
summary: Rodney McMullen, CEO of Kroger, discusses the company's response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including the significant acceleration of its online business and the challenges and adjustments made to the food supply chain. He highlights how the pandemic compressed years of digital growth into weeks and raised questions about optimal inventory levels.

title: How is Tractor Supply acing the pandemic?
summary: Tractor Supply Company reported strong second-quarter sales and plans to open new stores, attributing its success during the pandemic to long-term innovation, an understanding of physical stores as assets, and a customer-centric "customer as the channel" approach. The retailer emphasized key initiatives like an improved e-commerce platform, enhanced mobile shopping, and expanded delivery options, which allowed it to swiftly implement curbside pickup and ship-from-store services. Tractor Supply's success is presented as a case study for other retailers, highlighting the importance of customer segment clarity, integrated customer journeys beyond distinct channels, and a culture of agile experimentation.

title: Google to buy stake in ADT in home security push for $450 million
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is acquiring a 6.6% stake in ADT Inc. for $450 million to boost its home security presence and drive sales of its Nest devices. This investment gives ADT a high-profile technology partner and access to new resources, while Google gains access to ADT's 6.5 million customers. The companies plan to integrate Google products with ADT's services and co-invest an additional $150 million each in co-marketing, product development, technology, and employee training.

title: Capital One: What’s in an Empty Wallet?
summary: Capital One (COF) stock has been significantly impacted by the pandemic, with shares collapsing and only partially recovering. The company reported a net loss of $918 million in Q2, cut its marketing budget, and reduced its dividend by 75%. This financial distress, coupled with a major data breach, reflects the broader challenges faced by banks deeply involved in the credit card business during economic downturns.

title: Digital Realty submits plans for large Dulles data center campus
summary: Digital Realty has submitted plans for a large data center campus called 'Digital Dulles' in the Dulles International Airport area of Loudoun County, Virginia. The project encompasses several data centers and substations on a 433-acre property acquired in 2018. Construction is contingent on approval from the Army Corps of Engineers and public comments are being sought.

title: Introducing Cloudflare Network Interconnect
summary: Cloudflare announced Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI), allowing customers to directly link their branch and HQ locations with Cloudflare's network. This service offers enhanced security, reliability, and performance by bypassing the public internet for connectivity to Cloudflare's full suite of network functions. CNI supports various Cloudflare products like Access, CDN, Magic Transit, and Workers, providing a scalable and flexible solution for secure and optimized network integration globally.

title: Edgewell to Acquire Mass Grooming Brand Cremo
summary: Edgewell Personal Care Co. has announced its acquisition of men's grooming company Cremo for $235 million. This deal aims to bolster Edgewell's men's grooming portfolio, which already includes brands like Jack Black and Bulldog, and capitalize on the fast-growing segments within the market. The acquisition follows Edgewell's previously failed attempt to acquire Harry's and comes as Edgewell reports a 20.6 percent year-over-year decrease in fiscal third-quarter net sales.

title: Ford Motor Company gets new CEO on October 1st
summary: Jim Hackett is retiring as CEO of Ford Motor Company after three years, with current Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley taking over on October 1st, 2020. Farley aims for a 10% operating margin and acknowledges new competitors like Amazon, Baidu, Tesla, and Apple. He also faces the challenge of reviving Ford's declining car sales in China and navigating the company through the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

title: Apple marketing chief Phil Schiller steps down from role
summary: Phil Schiller, Apple's long-serving marketing boss, is stepping down from his role but will remain with the company as an "Apple Fellow," continuing to oversee the App Store and company events. Greg Joswiak, one of Schiller's deputies, will take over as vice president of worldwide marketing. Schiller's transition marks another high-profile executive change at Apple, coming amidst increased scrutiny over the App Store's policies.

title: Ford CEO Jim Hackett to retire; Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley will take helm
summary: Ford Motor Co. CEO Jim Hackett is retiring from his position, effective October 1, 2020, and will be succeeded by Chief Operating Officer Jim Farley. Hackett led the company since May 2017, overseeing a restructuring plan and challenges with product launches and stock value, while Farley is known as a "car guy" with a strong background in the auto industry and a focus on flawless product execution and an expanded affordable lineup. The transition comes as Ford faces intense competition and an evolving industry landscape, with many analysts and employees expressing optimism about Farley's leadership.

title: Connectivity with the consumer: The Honest Company’s formula for growth
summary: Nick Vlahos, CEO of The Honest Company, discusses the company's growth strategy, emphasizing connectivity with consumers and an omnichannel approach. He highlights the importance of responding to evolving consumer behaviors, particularly the demand for "better-for-you" and "clean" products, and details strategies for innovation, market expansion, and fostering customer loyalty. The article also touches on how Honest adapted its operations during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Ford's New CEO Names Amazon, Apple, Tesla, Baidu As Biggest Rivals
summary: Ford's incoming CEO, Jim Farley, has identified tech giants Amazon, Apple, Baidu, and Tesla, alongside Toyota, as the company's primary competitors, shifting focus away from traditional auto rivals like General Motors and Fiat Chrysler. Industry experts agree with Farley's assessment, noting significant investments by Silicon Valley companies in electric and self-driving vehicle technology. This new competitive landscape highlights the evolving nature of the automotive industry, demanding Ford to compete for talent and technological advancement against these innovative firms.

title: MTN seeking to sell stake in Africa’s biggest wireless carrier
summary: MTN Group Ltd. is planning to sell all or part of its $243 million stake in Jumia Technologies AG, an online retailer, to reduce debt and enter new markets. This move is part of MTN's broader strategy to dispose of non-core assets, having already generated R14 billion ($812 million) from previous sales. The company is also considering selling its 29% stake in IHS Towers and plans to bid for a license to enter the Ethiopian telecommunications market.

title: TTEC Signs Agreement to Acquire VoiceFoundry, Setting the Foundation for Significant Future Growth with Amazon Connect
summary: TTEC Holdings, Inc. announced an agreement to acquire VoiceFoundry, a global partner of Amazon Web Services, aiming to create an end-to-end CX delivery solution for Amazon Connect. This acquisition integrates Amazon Connect into TTEC's Humanify Cloud CX Ecosystem, offering clients enhanced customer experience applications and API integration. VoiceFoundry's expertise in AI and natural language automation, particularly with Amazon Connect, will expand TTEC Digital's cloud capabilities and client base in various sectors.

title: Bezos Sells $3.1 Billion of Amazon Shares After Wealth Jumps
summary: Jeff Bezos sold over $3.1 billion worth of Amazon.com Inc. shares, following an earlier sale of $4.1 billion this year. Despite this, the sale represents a small portion of his overall stake, as his wealth has significantly increased due to the surge in demand for Amazon's e-commerce services during the Covid-19 pandemic. The transactions were disclosed in SEC filings.

title: Google investment in ADT raises profile, competitive edge — plus data worries
summary: Google's $450 million investment in ADT Inc. will boost ADT's profile and allow it to sell and install Google's smart home devices, enhancing its competitive edge and customer experience. The partnership is expected to benefit ADT through Google's AI and data analytics expertise, although it also raises concerns about data privacy and market consolidation among tech giants.

title: EBay, Prova Group partner on sports memorabilia authentication
summary: EBay has partnered with Pro Football Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith and Prova Group to offer authentication services for sports memorabilia sold on its platform. Sellers can use Prova Group's verification service, receiving a Prova SmarTag linked to a document of authenticity. This partnership aims to combat counterfeit goods and increase buyer confidence in the sports memorabilia market, which has been a challenge for e-commerce platforms.

title: US financial regulator fines Capital One $80 million over data breach
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has fined Capital One $80 million in connection with a 2019 data breach that exposed details of approximately 106 million people. The fine addresses Capital One's failure to establish effective risk assessment processes before migrating to the cloud and not addressing deficiencies in a timely manner. Capital One states it has since invested significant resources to strengthen its cyber defenses.

title: #GapIncVotes: Raise Your Voice + Be Counted!
summary: Gap Inc. launched its #GapIncVotes initiative on the anniversary of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, committing to civic engagement and addressing systemic racism. The company will provide educational tools and inspiring stories, as well as offering up to three hours of paid time off for store employees to vote and a no-meetings day for headquarter staff. They encourage employees and customers to register to vote, check mail-in/early voting options, and complete the census.

title: Moderna Leverages AWS Cloud Platform to Develop New Class of Vaccines and Therapeutics
summary: Moderna has selected Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud provider for analytics and machine learning workloads to accelerate the development of its mRNA medicines. This partnership allows Moderna to quickly design research experiments, automate laboratory processes, and comply with regulations, leading to the rapid delivery of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate (mRNA-1273) to NIH for trials. By leveraging AWS, Moderna streamlines its drug discovery pipeline and manufacturing, enabling a new class of mRNA-based treatments for various diseases.

title: Capital One slapped with $80M fine for 2019 data hack
summary: Capital One has been fined $80 million by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency over a 2019 data breach that exposed the personal information of over 100 million people. The OCC stated Capital One failed to establish effective risk assessment processes before moving operations to the public cloud and did not correct deficiencies promptly. The bank is now required to enhance cybersecurity defenses and submit a plan to the Federal Reserve outlining these improvements.

title: Capital One to pay $80 million fine after data breach
summary: Capital One Financial Corp will pay an $80 million fine to a U.S. bank regulator following a massive data breach a year ago. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) penalized the bank for failing to adequately identify and manage risk related to moving operations to the cloud. The breach compromised personal information, including approximately 140,000 Social Security numbers and 80,000 linked bank account numbers.

title: Capital One to pay $80 million fine for 2019 hack that exposed 100 million accounts
summary: Capital One has agreed to pay an $80 million fine to settle federal charges related to a 2019 hack that exposed over 100 million credit card applications. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) found Capital One neglected to protect customer data and failed to establish effective risk assessment processes before migrating operations to the cloud. The company is also required to establish an independent committee to assess and address cybersecurity issues.

title: Thermo Fisher Scientific expands deployment model options for SampleManager LIMS software
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific has expanded its deployment options for SampleManager LIMS software, now offering end-to-end support in the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud. This new offering aims to significantly reduce the financial and human resource investment for laboratories, while providing secure and scalable access to data for improved decision-making and collaboration. The company emphasizes the robust data security measures in place, including its Corporate Information Security (CIS) program.

title: Bank OZK Seeks to Foreclose on David Edelstein’s Lincoln Road Buildings
summary: Bank OZK is seeking to foreclose on two Lincoln Road properties owned by developer David Edelstein, looking to collect on the remaining $12.8 million of a loan plus fees and interest. The suit alleges that loan guarantors, including Edelstein's TriStar Capital, have not made a payment since April. The bank's action highlights early commercial foreclosures in South Florida amidst a challenging period for Lincoln Road businesses.

title: Capital One Fined $80 Million for 2019 Data Breach Affecting 106 Million Users
summary: Capital One has been fined $80 million by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) for its 2019 data breach that exposed the personal information of over 106 million users. The fine was imposed due to Capital One's failure to establish appropriate risk management and security controls before migrating to a public cloud-based service, leading to the breach by a former Amazon Web Services employee. In addition to the monetary penalty, Capital One is required to enhance its cybersecurity defenses and submit a plan to the OCC within 90 days.

title: Buffett buys back record $5.1 billion in Berkshire stock as coronavirus hits operating earnings
summary: Berkshire Hathaway repurchased a record $5.1 billion of its own stock in May and June, the largest single buyback period for Warren Buffett's conglomerate. This occurred as operating profits fell 10% in the second quarter due to the coronavirus pandemic impacting businesses like Geico and Precision Castparts, though net earnings surged to $26.3 billion primarily from unrealized gains in public market investments. Buffett warned against focusing solely on these volatile net earnings due to the pandemic's ongoing uncertainties.

title: WarnerMedia’s New CEO Says HBO Max Has One Clear Edge Over Netflix
summary: WarnerMedia CEO Jason Kilar believes HBO Max has a distinct advantage over competitors like Netflix, focusing on quality content despite lacking an early breakout hit. Kilar, who previously led Hulu, aims to use this strategy to thwart rivals in the streaming landscape. The article notes his past experience at Hulu and Amazon and touches on the historical context of media companies' hesitance to embrace streaming.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Amazon and Mall Operator Look at Turning Sears, J.C. Penney Stores Into Fulfillment Centers
summary: Amazon and Simon Property Group, the largest mall owner in the U.S., are reportedly in discussions to convert vacant Sears and J.C. Penney stores into Amazon fulfillment centers. This move highlights the accelerating convergence of retail and logistics as traditional brick-and-mortar stores face decline. The potential partnership would repurpose large, underutilized commercial real estate for Amazon's distribution needs.

title: Amazon and mall owner Simon consider turning Sears, J.C. Penney stores into fulfillment centers
summary: Amazon and Simon Property Group are in discussions to convert former Sears and J.C. Penney department stores into Amazon fulfillment centers. This move would benefit Amazon by speeding up last-mile delivery and provide Simon with a steady tenant for struggling mall spaces. It represents a shift for mall owners willing to repurpose prime retail locations for logistics purposes.

title: Simon Property Group weighs empty mall spaces as Amazon centers
summary: Simon Property Group has been in discussions with Amazon to convert vacant mall spaces, previously occupied by anchor tenants like J.C. Penney and Sears, into Amazon fulfillment centers. This move would represent a significant shift for the mall business, potentially involving considerable rent discounts and altering foot traffic patterns, but could help revitalize struggling retail properties. The discussions began before the COVID-19 pandemic, and Amazon has also considered using J.C. Penney locations for its grocery stores.

title: Hasbro pulls Trolls doll from stores due to ‘inappropriately placed’ button
summary: Hasbro is removing its Trolls World Tour Giggle and Sing Poppy doll from stores due to public outcry over an "inappropriately placed" button. The doll has a sensor located in its crotch area that activates giggling and phrases when pressed, leading to a Change.org petition signed by nearly 500,000 people who found the feature problematic and suggesting it normalizes child molestation. Hasbro stated the feature was designed to react when the doll was seated and apologized, offering replacement dolls to consumers.

title: Gartner: IaaS Public Cloud Services Market Grew 37.3% In 2019
summary: The global infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) market for public cloud services saw a 37.3% growth in 2019, reaching $44.5 billion, with Amazon Web Services (AWS) maintaining its lead despite a slight market share decrease. Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud experienced significant growth, while Chinese providers Alibaba Cloud and Tencent also showed strong market expansion. Gartner plans to combine IaaS and PaaS into a new category called Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Services (CIPS) for future reporting to better reflect market realities.

title: |【2020最新】知的好奇心を刺激するアート(芸術)系アプリのおすすめ5選
summary: This article introduces five recommended art-related apps from 2020 that stimulate intellectual curiosity. It highlights apps like "DailyArt" for daily art discovery, "Ukiyo-e Wallpaper" for Japanese art backgrounds, "Magic Poser" for 3D model drawing references, "Chirashi Museum" for event leaflets, and "Happy Color" for number-based coloring puzzles. The article details features and benefits of each app, catering to both art education and entertainment.

title: With half of its business at retailers like Walmart and Amazon, Wrangler parent Kontoor Brands is ‘winning with the winners’
summary: Kontoor Brands Inc., parent company to Lee and Wrangler jeans, has seen its shares jump 23% over the past month. Over half of its business is conducted through essential retailers like Walmart, Target, Amazon, and Kohl's, which remained open during COVID-19 lockdowns, allowing the company to continue selling its products. While the stock is down by half for the year to date, its strong retail partnerships are proving beneficial.

title: With half of its business at retailers like Walmart and Amazon, Wrangler parent Kontoor Brands is ‘winning with the winners’
summary: Kontoor Brands Inc., parent company of Lee and Wrangler jeans, has seen its shares jump 23% over the past month despite being down by half for the year. The company conducts over half of its business with major retailers like Walmart, Target, Amazon, and Kohl’s. This strategic partnership with essential retailers allowed its products to remain accessible during COVID-19 lockdowns, contributing to its resilience in the market.

title: Healthcare Supply Chain Management Market May See Big Move |
summary: The "Global Healthcare Supply Chain Management Market Size, Status and Forecast 2019-2025" report by HTF MI evaluates the market, identifying opportunities and risks. It details market trends, drivers, technologies, and investment structures, profiling key players like SAP, Oracle, and McKesson. The study segments the market by product type (Supplier Management Software, Transportation Software, Procurement Software) and applications (Healthcare Providers, Suppliers, Distributors).

title: Simon Property Group and Amazon in Talks on Fulfillment Centers
summary: Simon Property Group, the largest mall owner, is reportedly in discussions with Amazon to convert vacant retail spaces, including former JCPenney and Sears stores, into Amazon fulfillment centers. This move could benefit Amazon by speeding up last-mile delivery and provide Simon with steady tenants, addressing challenges faced by malls. The article also provides a financial overview of both Simon Property Group and Amazon, including their stock performance, market capitalization, and analyst ratings.

title: Mall operator reportedly in talks to bring Amazon fulfillment centers to former J.C. Penney, Sears stores
summary: Amazon and Simon Property Group Inc., the largest mall owner in the U.S., reportedly discussed converting former J.C. Penney and Sears stores into Amazon fulfillment centers. These discussions, which began before the pandemic but accelerated due to the decline of malls and e-commerce boom, would allow Amazon to speed up delivery and provide Simon with steady tenants for struggling spaces. While details remain speculative, this move could significantly impact the retail landscape, offering a new purpose for vacant department store properties.

title: Bridgford Foods Hit by Netwalker Ransomware
summary: Our researchers identified a leak post in which the Netwalker ransomware operators claimed to have breached Bridgford Foods. The Netwalker group has also shared a few screenshots to support their claim, in which you can spot data folders and data files such as accounting, Amazon, Walmart, marketing-related data, payroll files, payment statements, and bank emails. It seems that the Netwalker ransomware group would tend to publish the company’s sensitive data within 29 days.

title: Banks and tech giants including JPMorgan and Amazon pledge to hire 100,000 minority and low-income New Yorkers
summary: A new organization called the New York Jobs CEO Council, comprising leaders from 27 firms including JPMorgan, IBM, and Amazon, has pledged to hire 100,000 people from low-income Black, Latino, and Asian communities by 2030. The initiative aims to address inequality exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic, providing entry-level jobs and apprenticeships, with 25,000 specifically for CUNY students. Co-chairs include Jamie Dimon, Arvind Krishna, and Julie Sweet, with support from other tech and finance giants.

title: Antitrust hawks, restaurants want to rein in food delivery apps
summary: An online campaign led by the American Economic Liberties Project is launching to limit the market power of food delivery apps like Grubhub and Uber Eats. The campaign aims to lobby local and state governments to cap fees charged by these apps, which restaurants contend are predatory, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, the campaign seeks Federal Trade Commission investigation into the companies for alleged anti-competitive practices.

title: Amazon to open multiple full-size grocery stores in Greater Washington. We've identified where.
summary: Amazon plans to open multiple full-size grocery stores in the Greater Washington area, distinct from its Whole Foods brand. These stores will be approximately 30,000 square feet each. The article, updated on August 12, 2020, indicates Amazon is actively expanding its grocery presence in the D.C. area.

title: Amazon expected to create largest metro Detroit location at former state fairgrounds site
summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to develop a 3.8 million-square-foot distribution center at the former Michigan state fairgrounds site in Detroit, a project valued at $400 million. This development, which would create 1,200 jobs, is a joint effort by Sterling Group and Hillwood Enterprises LP, who will pay $9 million for the land without city tax breaks. The plan requires Detroit City Council approval and would also include a new $7 million transit center paid for by the developers.

title: FuboTV begins streaming some content in 4K with HDR10
summary: FuboTV has started streaming select content, specifically main broadcasts of the 2018 FIFA World Cup, in 4K resolution with HDR10 support. This feature is initially available on Chromecast and Amazon Fire TV 4K devices, with support for Apple TV and Roku devices coming soon. FuboTV is the first virtual MVPD to launch 4K HDR in beta, requiring users to have compatible 4K HDR TVs, HDMI 2.0/2.2 ports, and sufficient bandwidth.

title: Jack in the Box Goes All-In on AWS
summary: Jack in the Box is migrating its entire IT infrastructure to Amazon Web Services (AWS), moving away from on-premises data centers to enhance flexibility, resilience, and operational efficiency across its 2,200+ restaurants. This transition involves utilizing AWS's cloud services, including Amazon RDS and Redshift, for data management, enabling advanced analytics for sales and inventory, and leveraging machine learning for improved customer service and personalized marketing. The move aims to innovate digital experiences, optimize operations, and better adapt to changing business conditions.

title: PPP likely saved 35 million jobs, says JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon estimates that the government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) saved between 30 to 35 million jobs by providing loans to small businesses affected by the coronavirus pandemic. Dimon praised the swift action of lawmakers and the administration, but also highlighted the need to extend the program, especially for minority-owned businesses that may not have initially received adequate funds. He also discussed the formation of the New York Jobs CEO Council to address the racial wealth gap and economic inequality, anticipating a delayed economic recession and stressing the importance of safely reopening the economy.

title: Payments giant Stripe poaches General Motors' CFO in its latest high-profile hire
summary: Payments company Stripe has hired General Motors' Chief Financial Officer Dhivya Suryadevara as it expands its executive team amidst a boom in e-commerce. Suryadevara, who led GM through a challenging financial period, will focus on aggressive growth while maintaining fiscal responsibility at Stripe. This move is part of a series of high-profile hires by Stripe, which has seen significant growth, especially during the pandemic, and is currently valued at $36 billion.

title: Hyundai, Aptiv Dub Autonomous Venture ‘Motional,’ Increase Hiring
summary: Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv Plc have named their autonomous-driving joint venture "Motional" and plan significant expansion. The company aims to increase staffing by 45% to over 1,000 people and have a self-driving car ready for testing by 2022. Motional seeks to sell its software to robotaxi fleets, leveraging Hyundai's backing to compete with tech giants entering the autonomous vehicle space.

title: Jack in the Box contains data in the cloud
summary: Jack in the Box has migrated its on-premises data centers to Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud infrastructure to enhance flexibility, resiliency, and customer experiences. This move allows the company to automate IT administration tasks, reduce costs, and leverage machine learning for deeper customer insights and operational efficiency. The fast-food retailer plans further AWS-based projects, including prediction of store-level customer traffic and optimization of service time and food costs, especially in response to increased mobile app and delivery service use during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Jamie Dimon of JP Morgan Chase and other CEOs aim to hire 100,000 New Yorkers by 2030
summary: A group of CEOs, led by Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase and the head of Google, formed the New York Jobs CEO Council with the goal of hiring 100,000 disadvantaged New Yorkers or people of color by 2030. This initiative aims to provide training, apprenticeships, and entry-level positions to address economic inequities exacerbated by the COVID-19 crisis, particularly in communities of color. The program, which includes companies like Goldman Sachs and Amazon, also plans to expand beyond entry-level roles and potentially to other cities.

title: Kroger goes for endless aisles with new marketplace strategy
summary: Kroger is expanding its ship-to-home service by launching a marketplace strategy that will initially offer over 50,000 products from third-party sellers, effectively doubling its current online assortment. This initiative focuses on specialty, natural, organic, and international products, as well as general merchandise, aiming to attract high-value shoppers and compete with other major retailers. Kroger has partnered with Mirakl and carefully vetted sellers to ensure product quality and enhance its e-commerce presence by integrating ship-to-home, delivery, and curbside pickup services.

title: Macerich posts $27M loss; CEO touts physical retail
summary: Mall landlord Macerich reported a $26.7 million net income loss in the second quarter of 2020, down significantly from a $13.9 million profit in the same period of 2019, as rent collection proved challenging during pandemic-induced mall closures. Despite acknowledging the financial hit, CEO Thomas O’Hern remained optimistic about physical retail, projecting better performance for the latter half of the year and downplaying the long-term impact of e-commerce. The company faced hurdles with declining rent collections and an acceleration of tenant bankruptcies but maintained that its leasing strategy remained unchanged.

title: Amazon Cometh: The 7,000 Units on the Boards Between Pentagon City and Potomac Yard
summary: This article details the extensive residential development pipeline in the "National Landing" area of northern Virginia, including Pentagon City and Potomac Yard, spurred by Amazon's presence. It highlights over 7,000 new residential units across various projects, outlining specific buildings, unit counts, retail components, and affordable housing commitments. The developments aim to transform the area with new housing, commercial spaces, and infrastructure in response to the increased demand.

title: Victoria’s Secret, PINK stores in Shrewsbury have permanently closed
summary: The Victoria's Secret and PINK stores in Shrewsbury, New Jersey, have permanently closed as of July 30, 2020. This closure is part of a larger plan by Victoria's Secret parent company, L Brands, to close about 250 stores in the U.S. and Canada in 2020. While 37 Victoria's Secret and 10 PINK stores remain in New Jersey, further closures in the state are uncertain.

title: Item Detection Camera From: Cognex Corporation
summary: Cognex Corporation has introduced the 3D-A1000 Item Detection System, a smart camera designed to identify objects on high-speed sorters. This system utilizes patented 3D Symbolic Light technology for precise 3D and 2D information without an encoder, allowing for quick installation and detailed inspections. It aims to improve the accuracy and speed of sorting systems for retailers.

title: Departure of GM CFO Dhivya Suryadevara highlights ongoing 'brain drain' problem for auto industry
summary: The departure of GM CFO Dhivya Suryadevara to digital payments company Stripe highlights a growing "brain drain" problem for traditional automakers like GM and Ford. As the automotive and tech sectors increasingly collide, these companies struggle with talent acquisition and retention, losing seasoned executives and promising mid-career professionals to tech firms and startups. This trend is exacerbated by a perceived lack of appeal in the automotive industry compared to the innovative allure of the tech sector.

title: Amazon and Google among big US companies pledging to hire 100,000 people from marginalized New York communities
summary: Major US companies including Amazon, Google, and Goldman Sachs have pledged to hire 100,000 people from New York City's low-income and minority communities by 2030. This initiative, called the New York Jobs CEO Council, aims to address racial and economic inequities worsened by COVID-19 by providing entry-level positions, apprenticeships, and on-the-job learning. While the effort is praised as a good start, experts emphasize the need for specific interventions like mentoring programs and performance reviews to ensure career advancement for employees from underrepresented backgrounds beyond entry-level roles.

title: P&G trials Olay refill pods: ‘Small steps can lead to monumental change’, says exec
summary: Procter & Gamble is launching Olay refill pods for its Regenerist Whip moisturiser on Amazon UK, marking its first European foray after a North American trial. These recyclable pods aim to reduce plastic waste and promote sustainability in beauty. P&G views this initiative as a "first step" towards more sustainable packaging and is partnering with Young Women's Trust, donating £5 from each purchase to support young women.

title: Sonos Move vs. Bose Portable Smart Speaker: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares the Sonos Move and Bose Portable Smart Speaker, highlighting their pros, cons, and key features to help consumers choose the best option based on their priorities. The Sonos Move offers Apple Music support and an included charging dock, while the Bose speaker is more portable, lighter, and has a longer battery life at a lower price. Ultimately, the choice depends on whether convenience and Apple Music compatibility (Sonos Move) or portability and price (Bose) are more important to the buyer.

title: Apple Sells $5.5 Billion of Bonds in Tech Borrowing Boom
summary: Apple Inc. has sold $5.5 billion in bonds, joining a trend of tech giants leveraging low borrowing costs. This marks Apple's second bond issuance in a single calendar year since 2017, a strategy also pursued by companies like Amazon and Alphabet. The move highlights the current environment where cash-rich companies are taking advantage of historically low yields to raise capital.

title: Disney, Netflix Sue Streaming Service for Copyright Infringement
summary: Disney, Netflix, and other major media companies have filed a lawsuit against Florida-based Crystal Clear Media, alleging copyright infringement. The lawsuit, filed in a U.S. District Court in California, claims that Crystal Clear Media illegally offers copyrighted movies and television programs online for a fee, including popular titles like "Frozen II" and "The Amazing Spider-Man."

title: CarParts.com Reports Big Second Quarter
summary: CarParts.com reported a strong second quarter with revenue increasing 61% to $118.9 million and a net income of $1.6 million. CEO Lev Peker attributed this growth to pandemic-related factors, including consumers opting for DIY car repairs and driving personal vehicles more. The company also recently changed its name from U.S. Auto Parts Network Inc. to CarParts.com Inc. to better reflect its identity as a technology company in the auto parts business.

title: US retailers take on Amazon, eBay over counterfeit goods
summary: A new coalition formed by major US retailers like Walmart and Target is pushing for legislation to compel e-commerce giants such as Amazon and eBay to better verify third-party sellers and combat counterfeit goods. The "Buy Safe America Coalition" supports the INFORM Consumers Act, which would require digital marketplaces to collect and disclose more detailed information about high-volume sellers. This initiative comes amidst growing concerns about fake products online, a problem that has intensified during the pandemic-driven surge in e-commerce, and follows previous calls from lawmakers and the White House for stronger measures.

title: The post-COVID economy
summary: This article examines four key trends that are likely to shape the global economy after the COVID-19 pandemic: the acceleration of de-globalization, the reversal of hypermobility and agglomeration, the acceleration of automation and digitization, and increased demand for green policies. It discusses how the pandemic intensified existing trends and reversed others, impacting trade, travel, urbanization, and technology adoption, with significant macroeconomic implications.

title: GIB - CGI Inc Latest Stock News & Market Updates
summary: This page provides the latest news and insights on CGI Inc. (GIB), a global IT and business consulting firm. It covers company announcements on technology initiatives, government contracts, acquisitions, and regulatory disclosures. Recent updates include CGI's expansion in Atlanta, director election results, Q1 Fiscal 2026 earnings, renewal of its Normal Course Issuer Bid, and strategic collaborations with OpenAI and Google Cloud for advanced AI solutions.

title: Macy's closing 100 stores nationwide, locations unknown
summary: Macy's announced plans to close approximately 100 stores nationwide, representing about 14% of its total locations, by early 2017. The department store chain aims to invest more in online shopping and create a more energized experience in its remaining stores. While specific locations to be closed were not disclosed, Macy's stated that employees affected by the closures would be given opportunities to transfer to other stores if possible.

title: More than a dozen Massachusetts malls could be transformed as part of deal with Amazon
summary: Amazon.com Inc. and mall owner Simon Property Group Inc. are discussing a deal to transform vacant or occupied Sears and JCPenney locations within Simon malls into Amazon distribution hubs. This potential agreement could significantly impact Massachusetts commercial real estate, as Simon owns 14 properties in the state, five of which currently host Sears or JCPenney stores. Amazon is already a major industrial tenant in Greater Boston and continues to expand its distribution and delivery operations in the region.

title: Chewy Founder Ryan Cohen, Who Sold His Company For $3 Billion, Shares His Best Advice
summary: Ryan Cohen, founder of Chewy, shares his entrepreneurial journey, including overcoming 100 investor rejections and successfully building Chewy into a multi-billion dollar online pet retailer. He emphasizes customer obsession, strategic risk-taking, and the timeless advice from his father to prioritize customer happiness over immediate profit.

title: Roku Stock In 3 Years: What's Possible?
summary: This article analyzes Roku's stock potential over the next three years, predicting significant revenue growth and a potential return to profitability by 2022. Driven by an expanding user base and increasing advertising revenue, Roku's market cap could reach $27 billion, representing a 50% stock price increase. The analysis suggests that while the company is currently posting losses, its growth trajectory and P/S multiple make it an attractive investment.

title: Home Depot Doubles Comp. Sale Growth Rate in Q2 Due to Remodeling Amid COVID
summary: Home Depot saw its comparable sales double in Q2 2020 due to a surge in home remodeling projects during the COVID-19 pandemic, despite canceling typical spring sales events. The company adapted its business model, moving away from usual growth indicators like GDP and housing data, as customers used stimulus checks and saved money from other activities to fund home improvements. This unexpected boost highlights a shift in consumer behavior and retail dynamics during the pandemic, benefiting major home improvement retailers while other sectors struggled.

title: JD Logistics opens automated warehouse for bulky items, launches 1-hour delivery
summary: JD Logistics has expanded its operations by opening a new automated warehouse near Beijing, designed to handle bulky items like appliances and furniture, significantly boosting efficiency. This initiative, alongside a 33.8% increase in Q2 revenue for JD Logistics, highlights the company's continuous investments in technology and infrastructure. Additionally, JD.com launched a one-hour "Instant Delivery" service, further solidifying its position in the competitive e-commerce logistics market.

title: Nvidia Expands Partner Program With New Incentives, Training
summary: Nvidia has enhanced its Partner Network with new incentives, industry-specific training, and improved sales tracking for its growing channel of over 1,500 members. Key additions include a fixed back-end rebate for Elite partners, dedicated market development funds, and an expanded "AI Champions Club." The company is also planning future expansions, such as integrating Mellanox and Cumulus Networks' partner programs and introducing a cloud service provider program.

title: EY and Procter & Gamble team up on supply chain offering
summary: EY and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have broadened their alliance to offer supply chain expertise, combining their strengths to help businesses navigate challenges, particularly those exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic. This collaboration will address various supply chain processes, including strategy, planning, and distribution, leveraging advanced tools and joint teams. P&G, recognized for its leading supply chain operations, aims to share its successful methodologies with clients through EY to enhance responsiveness, productivity, and cost savings.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Launches hum by Colgate: The New Smart Electric Toothbrush that Guides Users to Brush Better and Get In Sync with Their Smile
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has launched hum by Colgate, a new smart electric toothbrush designed to help users improve their brushing habits. The toothbrush features smart sensors that track brushing frequency, duration, and coverage, providing personalized guidance and helping users achieve 50% better brushing efficacy. The accompanying app offers rewards through "Smile points" and integrates with the Apple Health app for a holistic wellness experience.

title: Exclusive: Amazon in talks to invest in cloud services company Rackspace - sources
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly in preliminary discussions to acquire a minority stake in U.S. cloud services provider Rackspace Technology Inc. This potential investment would strengthen ties between the two companies, as Rackspace already assists businesses in migrating data to Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and VMware. Rackspace's shares surged following the news of the possible deal, which would be the second such investment by a major tech company into an Apollo-owned firm this year, following Google's investment in ADT Inc.

title: 'Project Smile': Is Amazon expanding in St. Louis?
summary: St. Louis-based CRG is developing a 36-acre site in St. Peters, which many in the commercial real estate industry believe will become a last-mile warehouse and distribution facility for Amazon. The project, codenamed "Project Smile," involves a 142,600-square-foot building and parking for 983 delivery vans. While Amazon and CRG have declined to comment, officials at a St. Peters planning and zoning meeting referred to it as a "delivery station building," a term Amazon uses for its last-mile facilities.

title: SoftBank builds $1.2 billion Amazon stake; invests in Netflix, Tesla
summary: SoftBank Group Corp has built a $1.2 billion stake in Amazon and also invested in Netflix, Tesla, Microsoft, and Alphabet, marking a strategic shift towards liquid stocks. This move comes as the company expands its investment activities beyond unlisted startups and its Vision Fund, which has recently seen its holdings fall below acquisition prices. The group is leveraging a massive asset sale program to buy shares in these tech giants, whose values are currently rising amidst a tech stock rally.

title: Northrop Grumman enters solar deal with Dominion Energy
summary: Northrop Grumman has entered into a long-term contract with Dominion Energy to purchase solar energy from the 62.5-megawatt Madison Solar generating facility in Orange County. This agreement will offset 100% of Northrop Grumman’s manufacturing and office operations in Virginia, aligning with the company's commitment to environmental sustainability. Dominion Energy acquired the facility from Cypress Creek Renewables and aims to meet Virginia's clean economy goals by adding substantial solar generating capacity over the next 15 years.

title: The race to quantum advantage
summary: This article discusses the global race toward quantum advantage, highlighting how quantum computing promises to solve currently intractable problems across various industries. It details the fundamental concepts of quantum computing, including qubits and modalities like superconducting and trapped ion qubits, and outlines the technological stack required. The authors emphasize that while significant progress has been made by companies like IBM, Google, and Honeywell, the journey to scalable, error-free quantum computers capable of widespread application is still a marathon.

title: FedEx tacks on peak fees during holiday season
summary: FedEx is implementing new peak fees during the upcoming holiday season, charging customers between $1 and $5 per express or ground package. This decision comes as the carrier anticipates a surge in residential deliveries and increased operating costs due to high demand, exacerbated by the ongoing impact of the pandemic. The U.S. Postal Service is also adding similar fees to manage the expected increase in online holiday orders.

title: Amazon postal deal that Trump despises is actually profitable
summary: President Trump has frequently criticized the pricing agreement between Amazon and the U.S. Postal Service, claiming it leads to losses for the USPS. However, the Postal Service and lawmakers maintain that commercial package delivery, including deals with Amazon, FedEx, and UPS, is a lucrative segment, contradicting Trump's assertions. The Amazon deal, while confidential, has been described as profitable for the USPS, especially for "last mile" deliveries, and shipping and packages represented the only revenue growth segment for the agency in Q3 2020.

title: AWS Announces General Availability of Its Quantum Algorithm Design Service
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced the general availability of Amazon Braket, a fully managed service designed to help customers explore and design quantum algorithms. Amazon Braket allows users to test algorithms on simulated quantum computers and then run them on actual quantum processors from providers like D-Wave, IonQ, and Rigetti, using a unified development environment. This service aims to democratize access to quantum computing, helping researchers and businesses develop skills and explore potential applications without needing extensive in-house expertise or managing multiple vendor relationships.

title: COVID-19 Update: Amazon to Add 100 Jobs in Detroit, Novi’s Shyft Group Expands EV Production, Used Car and Trade-in Values Spiking During Pandemic, and More
summary: Amazon plans to add over 100 tech and corporate jobs in Detroit, expanding its Tech Hub with new office space. Novi-based Shyft Group is increasing electric vehicle production for parcel delivery, with initial deliveries expected in 2021. Meanwhile, used car and trade-in values are surging due to limited new vehicle inventory and high demand, while shelf-stable and frozen food sales have seen a revitalization during the pandemic.

title: Report: Amazon looks to acquire stake in San Antonio’s Rackspace Technology
summary: Amazon is reportedly in talks to acquire a minority stake in San Antonio cloud-computing company Rackspace Technology Inc., less than two weeks after Rackspace's $703 million initial public offering. This potential investment highlights Amazon's valuation of Rackspace's cloud capabilities and the growing demand for managed services on cloud infrastructure, according to industry analyst Philbert Shih. Rackspace's stock, trading as "RXT," saw a more than 10 percent increase on the news, closing Monday at $18.31.

title: Wayfair is on S&P’s ‘most vulnerable’ list despite soaring stock, new customer numbers
summary: Wayfair Inc. has been included in S&P Global Market Intelligence’s list of "Most Vulnerable Public American Retailers," despite recently reporting significant growth in new customers and soaring sales. As of August 14, S&P estimates Wayfair's one-year probability of default at 18.6% and two-year probability of default at 24%, highlighting financial concerns despite its e-commerce success. Blue Apron and J.Jill are also named on this list.

title: Why Kohl’s CEO thinks the retailer can win market share amid the COVID carnage
summary: Kohl's CEO Michelle Gass believes the retailer can gain market share despite a 23% sales drop in Q2, leveraging its strong balance sheet and rivals' bankruptcies. The company's strategy includes targeting customers from closed stores, growing partnerships with national brands like Under Armour and Nike, and emphasizing a spacious, uncluttered store environment to address health and safety concerns. However, Kohl's remains vulnerable as an apparel-heavy chain, reporting a Q2 loss while other retailers like Walmart and Home Depot saw strong results.

title: Amazon makes it harder for sellers to avoid shipping service
summary: Amazon is implementing new shipping performance requirements for third-party sellers, including Saturday deliveries and stricter one- and two-day delivery pledges, making it harder for them to avoid using Amazon's own shipping services. Merchants not meeting these targets risk losing the Prime fast-shipping badge. Critics argue this move has antitrust implications, potentially forcing sellers to use Amazon's more expensive logistics and raise product prices, effectively pushing them into Fulfillment By Amazon.

title: Beachbody Super Trainer And Nutrition Expert Autumn Calabrese Refuses To Let Personal Struggles Hold People Back From Success In New Book
summary: Beachbody Super Trainer and nutrition expert Autumn Calabrese has released a new book titled "Lose Weight Like Crazy: Even If You Have A Crazy Life," which details her personal journey and breakthrough approach to weight loss. The book shares a 30-day plan, new strategies, recipes, and workouts to help people overcome excuses and achieve their fitness goals by turning setbacks into opportunities. Calabrese shares her own struggles to empower readers to find their strength and make lasting positive changes in their lives.

title: TikTok Competitor BIGO to Relocate Its Hong Kong Servers in Singapore to Escape Crossfire
summary: BIGO, a Chinese short video service company backed by JOYY, is relocating its servers from Hong Kong to Singapore to emphasize its independence from its Chinese parent company. This move comes amidst international scrutiny on its competitor TikTok and rising geopolitical tensions that led to BIGO's apps being banned in India. JOYY's financial results for Q2 2020 showed significant growth in overseas users for its products, including Bigo Live and Likee.

title: The Inside Story Of Robinhood’s Billionaire Founders, Option Kid Cowboys And The Wall Street Sharks That Feed On Them
summary: This article delves into Robinhood's rapid rise, driven by commission-free trading and a surge of novice investors during the pandemic, and reveals its controversial business model of selling customer order flow to high-frequency trading firms. It explores how this model, while minting billionaire founders, prioritizes profit from sophisticated market makers, potentially at the expense of inexperienced traders. The piece also highlights the platform's challenges, including outages and the tragic death of a user, leading to calls for better regulation and education.

title: Nvidia earnings beat expectations, its data center business is bigger than its gaming business for the first time ever
summary: Nvidia reported better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings, with overall revenue up 50% year-over-year. For the first time, its data center business, driven by AI workloads and the Mellanox acquisition, surpassed its gaming unit in revenue. CEO Jensen Huang anticipates a strong second half for gaming, despite declines in professional visualization and automotive segments due to the pandemic.

title: Amazon cuts ties with Philadelphia and Pittsburgh-area delivery services; hundreds of jobs affected
summary: Amazon has cut contracts with several delivery companies in the Philadelphia and Pittsburgh areas, leading to the layoff of more than 600 workers. Companies like Prime EFS, Deliverol, and Courier Distribution Systems were affected, with Courier Distribution Systems alone laying off 64 workers in Sewickley. These job terminations are part of a larger trend affecting delivery companies across Pennsylvania.

title: Apple becomes US' first $2T company
summary: Apple Inc. has become the first U.S. company to achieve a $2 trillion market capitalization, with its share price climbing above $467.77. This milestone follows its previous achievement of being the first U.S. company to reach a $1 trillion market cap just over two years prior. The tech giant's market cap soared by 59% this year, joining Saudi Aramco as the only other company globally to reach this valuation.

title: Apple's $2 trillion value is proof that Tim Cook's services plan worked
summary: Apple reached a $2 trillion valuation, largely symbolic but indicative of CEO Tim Cook's successful pivot towards a services-led business model. Investors are increasingly valuing Apple like a software company, reflected in its rising P-E ratio, as the company diversified its revenue streams beyond hardware. This shift helped Apple double its value in just over two years, despite challenges like App Store criticism and dependence on its existing device base.

title: Apple Becomes First U.S. Company Worth More Than $2 Trillion
summary: Apple achieved a new financial milestone, becoming the first publicly traded U.S. company to reach a market capitalization of over $2 trillion. This valuation marks a doubling in just two years, driven by a strong stock performance, especially during the pandemic due to work-from-home trends and robust online sales. The company's market cap now surpasses that of other U.S. tech giants and the GDP of several developed countries, with a four-for-one stock split planned to make shares more accessible.

title: Big-Box Retailers’ Profits Surge as Pandemic Marches On (Published 2020)
summary: Walmart, Target, and other big-box retailers experienced a significant surge in profits during the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by their one-stop shopping convenience and e-commerce growth. Target reported its greatest quarterly sales increase in company history, while Walmart doubled its e-commerce sales and Home Depot saw sales rise over 23 percent. This success stands in contrast to many other retail sectors that faced bankruptcies during the same period.

title: The Sonos Arc is incredible but check your HDMI ports first
summary: The Sonos Arc soundbar offers incredibly spacious sound and Dolby Atmos support, making it one of the best premium soundbars available. However, its high price and reliance on a single HDMI eARC port for optimal performance, potentially limiting connectivity for other devices, are key considerations. Despite these factors, its impressive audio quality and smart features make it a strong contender for those seeking an immersive home audio experience.

title: Postal Service issues have affected Netflix and Amazon
summary: The U.S. Postal Service's operational issues have caused isolated delivery delays for Netflix's DVD-by-mail service, which still serves over 2 million subscribers. Amazon's e-commerce deliveries have also faced similar challenges. While these issues have generated concern, particularly regarding the November elections, they are not expected to materially impact Netflix's customer service or sales.

title: Apple is valued at $2 trillion as investor confidence grows
summary: Apple Inc. reached a market valuation of over $2 trillion in August 2020, just two years after hitting $1 trillion. This surge is attributed to growing investor confidence in Apple's shift toward services and surprisingly strong quarterly results despite the pandemic, with its stock up 57% year-to-date at the time. The company's market capitalization now rivals the combined value of the S&P 500's 200 smallest companies.

title: To get skin tones right, Pinterest’s AI went way beyond facial recognition
summary: Pinterest has updated its AI to more accurately detect skin tones in a wider array of images, moving beyond facial recognition. This helps users find more relevant beauty and style tips, and supports features like their augmented-reality Try On tool. The new system avoids biases associated with facial recognition and can analyze images beyond just faces, such as close-ups of body parts or accessories.

title: Amazon expected to occupy full building at WestPark 85 industrial development
summary: Amazon is anticipated to open a new distribution center within the WestPark 85 industrial development, situated near Charlotte Douglas International Airport. This move suggests further expansion of Amazon's presence in the Charlotte area, following other developments and hirings previously reported.

title: Amazon Names Logistics Head Dave Clark New Consumer CEO
summary: Amazon has appointed Dave Clark, previously its logistics chief, as the new CEO of its Worldwide Consumer unit, succeeding Jeff Wilke who plans to retire in Q1 2021. Clark, instrumental in building Amazon's vast logistics network, will now oversee the company's core retail website and its expanding delivery operations. His appointment comes as a surprise given Wilke was considered a potential successor to CEO Jeff Bezos.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club rolls out curbside pickup at all locations
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club has launched contactless curbside pickup at all 219 of its warehouse clubs across 17 states to enhance COVID-19 safety and customer convenience. The company also expanded its buy-online-pickup-in-club (BOPIC) service to include fresh and frozen foods, with a full rollout expected by the end of October. These initiatives build on BJ's efforts to improve its e-commerce offerings, which contributed significantly to its 24.2% merchandise comparable-sales growth in the second quarter.

title: Claims asserting Amazon’s algorithms commit direct copyright infringement survive Motion to Dismiss
summary: A federal district court in Northern California has allowed Williams-Sonoma to proceed with direct copyright infringement claims against Amazon.com, Inc. The case alleges that Amazon's algorithms selected and displayed copyrighted images of Williams-Sonoma's products on product detail pages without human intervention. The court denied Amazon's motion to dismiss, ruling that Williams-Sonoma sufficiently alleged "volitional conduct" on Amazon's part, given how its algorithms actively select content for publication.

title: Is Amazon teeing up another facility in Charlotte?
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly planning to lease a new 566,800-square-foot industrial warehouse at WestPark 85, near Charlotte Douglas International Airport. This move would add to Amazon's existing distribution and delivery facilities in the Charlotte region, indicating further expansion in the area. The building's groundbreaking occurred in early 2019 as the second phase of the project.

title: Starbucks, Dollar Tree to open soon at Morton Grove’s Sawmill Station, grocery store still unnamed: Village official
summary: Starbucks and Dollar Tree are slated to open in early fall at Morton Grove's new Sawmill Station commercial development, according to a village official. The identity of a proposed grocery store at the location remains undisclosed as of August 21, with the development team not yet revealing its name or an opening date. Other businesses like Raising Cane’s, Aspen Dental, Kohl’s, Cooper’s Hawk, LA. Fitness, and Ross are also expected to open in phases at Sawmill Station, which will also include rental apartments.

title: 24 Awesome Chapter Book Series for Kids
summary: This article lists 24 popular chapter book series for children, ranging from classics to more recent hits. It provides a brief description of each series, target age group, author, and an image of the book cover, making it a useful resource for parents and educators looking for reading recommendations. The selections cover various genres like fantasy, mystery, and humor, ensuring there's something for every young reader.

title: The Supply Side: Kate’s Real Food energy bars now in 1,000 Walmart stores
summary: Kate’s Real Food energy bars are now available in approximately 1,000 Walmart stores, a move stemming from a Walmart executive trying the product in Wyoming. The company, founded by Kate Schade, emphasizes certified organic, gluten-free, soy-free, and artificial ingredient-free recipes. This expansion into Walmart provides the small brand with its first national exposure and aligns with Walmart's goal of offering more affordable organic foods.

title: This Retail ETF Strategy Is Crushing it this Year
summary: The article highlights the success of the ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX), which has achieved an over 87% year-to-date gain by capitalizing on both the growth of e-commerce and the decline of brick-and-mortar retail. The strategy benefits from increased online sales and widespread store closures and bankruptcies among traditional retailers. Recent data indicate a significant surge in e-commerce sales, underscoring the fund's continued potential.

title: Inside Office Depot's Reinvention As a B2B Distributor
summary: Office Depot has been actively transforming its business model to prioritize B2B distribution channels over consumer retail for the past three years. Despite challenges from COVID-19, the company continues to invest in its Business Solutions Division and has undergone a holding company reorganization to further "Maximize B2B" efforts, as reflected in its evolving self-description and financial performance.

title: (08/25/20) Dan Sullivan: Technical Talk from The Chartist
summary: Despite high price-to-earnings multiples and near-historic valuations, technical expert Dan Sullivan believes the bull market has further to run, supported by bullish chart patterns and strong AIII sentiment indicators. He notes the significant outperformance of FAANG stocks relative to the S&P 500 and recommends Veeva Systems (VEEV) and DexCom (DXCM) in the medical sector for traders.

title: Amazon's Audible debuts cheaper, R134-a-month service
summary: Amazon's Audible is launching a more affordable service called Audible Plus for $7.95 (R134) a month, aiming to attract podcast listeners and expand beyond audiobooks. This new plan offers over 11,000 titles, including original series from various artists and actors, and is a strategic move to compete with platforms like Spotify in the non-music audio market. The initiative seeks to make Audible a daily destination for listeners with its extensive library, moving beyond its previous credit-based subscription model.

title: Get a pair of artfully ripped jeans for 25% off at Urban Outfitters
summary: Urban Outfitters is offering 25% off their exclusive BDG denim collection for both men and women, including a wide selection of ripped jeans that are currently on-trend. Non-ripped jean styles are also available in the sale. The discount is automatically applied at checkout, allowing customers to stock up on various BDG jeans, jackets, tees, and accessories.

title: B.C.’s back-to-school spending shifts to technology
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically altered annual back-to-school shopping in B.C., leading to a significant shift towards technology spending. Retailers are observing increased purchases of computers, tablets, and related accessories, while traditional school supplies like pens and paper, along with apparel, are seeing reduced demand. This shift is driven by the acceleration of online learning, with students needing to upgrade devices for virtual classes.

title: Etsy CEO says Amazon is trying to 'wipe out its competitors' by backing California consumer protection bill
summary: Etsy CEO Josh Silverman argues that Amazon's support for California's AB 3262 consumer protection bill is an anti-competitive tactic designed to burden small businesses with legal costs, effectively eliminating competitors. Amazon maintains it would support the bill if expanded to include all online marketplaces, regardless of their business models. The bill aims to hold online marketplaces liable for defective goods, a notable shift given Amazon's historical stance of being merely a conduit between buyers and sellers.

title: TUBI NOW AVAILABLE ON NEW TIVO STREAM 4K DEVICE AND STREAMING ON TIVO+
summary: Tubi, a division of FOX Entertainment, has announced that its library of over 23,000 movies and TV shows is now available on the new TiVo Stream 4K device and streaming on the TiVo+ content network. This renewed agreement allows TiVo customers to access Tubi's on-demand content for free, including new titles like Magic Mike XXL and The Family That Preys. The partnership aims to enhance content discovery and expand Tubi's reach across various platforms.

title: Amazon's latest grocery store concept opens, with high-tech carts
summary: Amazon has opened a new Amazon Fresh grocery store in Los Angeles, featuring "Amazon Dash Carts" that allow customers to skip checkout lines. This new store concept aims to expand Amazon's physical retail presence and compete with established grocery chains, focusing on national brands and offering lower prices. The technology-driven store also includes counters for web order pick-up/returns and Alexa-enabled stations.

title: Cetus: Cryptojacking Worm Targeting Docker Daemons
summary: A new cryptojacking worm named Cetus has been discovered, specifically targeting unsecured Docker daemons to mine Monero. Cetus, created by TeamTnT, disguises itself as legitimate Docker binaries like Portainer and uses Masscan to spread across networks. Palo Alto Networks customers are protected through Prisma Cloud Compute's host compliance protection feature.

title: Atlanta developer closes on land, secures $44M construction loan for Home Depot's new Hillsborough warehouse
summary: An Atlanta developer has successfully closed on the land and secured a $44 million construction loan for Home Depot's new warehouse in Hillsborough County, Florida. This development signifies the progress of Home Depot's Gibsonton warehouse project, with the same developer also constructing a warehouse for Amazon in Temple Terrace.

title: It’s Too Soon to Tune Out of QVC
summary: Qurate Retail, owner of QVC and HSN, has shown resilience despite challenges in the retail sector. The company successfully grew sales by 10% in the quarter ended June 30, beating estimates, even as many traditional retailers faced bankruptcy. This indicates that while TV-based home shopping may not be a future trend, Qurate is adapting effectively to current market conditions.

title: Soon, the Kitty Litter Will Come by Electric Truck (Published 2020)
summary: Major delivery carriers like UPS, FedEx, and Amazon are intensifying their efforts to electrify their vehicle fleets in response to surging delivery demand during the pandemic. This push is driven by concerns about climate change, rising delivery costs, government regulations, and significant advancements in battery technology, which are making electric vehicles more cost-effective. Industry analysts predict a substantial increase in electric delivery van orders as the economics of EVs become more favorable than diesel for short, local delivery operations.

title: Celsius notches another earnings record
summary: Celsius Holdings reported record revenue in the second quarter of 2020, reaching $30 million, an 86% increase over the same period in 2019. The company is nearing nationwide distribution in North America and has become the third largest energy drink seller on Amazon. Despite a recent private placement diluting shares, the company is well-capitalized and aims to eliminate outstanding bonds and fund growth opportunities.

title: Investing basics: what is a stock split?
summary: This article explains what a stock split is and how it impacts investors, using recent announcements from Apple and Tesla as examples. It clarifies that while a split increases the number of shares and reduces the per-share price, it does not change the company's fundamental value or an investor's total holdings. The piece also briefly covers the concept of a reverse stock split.

title: Amazon's sustainability initiatives: Half empty or half full?
summary: Amazon's sustainability efforts, including a $2 billion Climate Pledge Fund and investments in renewable energy, are met with mixed reviews regarding their effectiveness and sincerity. While some experts praise the scale of Amazon's initiatives, others, including sustainability ranking firms and environmental activists, criticize the company's overall environmental impact and practices. The article highlights the ongoing tension between profit-driven business models and environmental activism in evaluating corporate sustainability.

title: FedEx Hiring for Indy Hub
summary: FedEx (NYSE: FDX) is hosting a hiring event at its Indianapolis International Airport hub to fill permanent part-time package handling positions. The company is looking to meet ongoing demand for e-commerce shipments, offering starting rates between $18.30-$19.12 per hour, with a night shift premium and comprehensive benefits. Individuals unable to attend the event are encouraged to apply online.

title: Exclusive: -Facebook says Apple rejected its attempt to tell users about App Store fees
summary: Facebook stated that Apple rejected its attempt to inform users about the 30% App Store fee on sales from a new online events feature, citing a rule against "irrelevant" information. Facebook had sought a fee waiver from Apple for small businesses using the feature to recover COVID-19 related revenue losses, but Apple declined. This incident aligns Facebook with other developers, like Epic Games, who are criticizing Apple's App Store commissions and facing scrutiny over alleged anti-competitive behavior.

title: Uh Oh, Here’s Why the Internet Broke Again
summary: A widespread internet outage on Sunday morning impacting Cloudflare, PlayStation Network, Xbox Live, Amazon, and Hulu was attributed to a single internet service provider, CenturyLink. Cloudflare, which provides online security services, went down after issues with a "third-party transit provider" (CenturyLink) caused HTTP 5xx errors across its data centers. CenturyLink confirmed and resolved an IP outage, apologizing for the significant disruption it caused across the U.S. and Western Europe.

title: Mark Cuban's Strategy Returned 1,000% on Netflix and 500% on Amazon
summary: Billionaire investor Mark Cuban revealed his successful buy-and-hold strategy, which yielded a 1,000% return on Netflix and a 500% return on Amazon. Cuban explained that he sticks with companies he believes in and unlike his past self, he no longer actively trades due to increased capital chasing fewer stocks. He also noted that economic uncertainty from the pandemic creates new opportunities for innovation, particularly in the digital sector.

title: SMB and NFS? Cloud Volumes for AWS Has You Covered
summary: This article discusses how NetApp Cloud Volumes Service for AWS simplifies file sharing protocols by supporting NFS, SMB, or both within a single volume creation service. It highlights the benefits of using Cloud Volumes Service for unified file sharing, including migration without refactoring, continuous upgrades, on-demand provisioning, and cost savings compared to using separate services like Amazon EFS and FSx for Windows Server. The service allows users to easily create and manage dual-protocol volumes on AWS.

title: Tesla, Apple stock splits pave way for more gains
summary: Apple and Tesla's recent stock splits may lead to further share price gains by increasing affordability for smaller investors, despite splits not changing a company's overall market capitalization. Historically, major brands have seen an average 33% share price rally within 12 months post-split. While some experts caution about increased volatility and diluted earnings, others predict continued growth for mega-cap tech stocks.

title: Building smarter products with sensors
summary: This article discusses how sensors are becoming foundational to building intelligent products across various industries. It highlights key technological trends such as miniaturization, sensor fusion, and low-power silicon that are enhancing sensor performance. The piece emphasizes the importance of integrating these technologies to improve product efficiency, safety, and precision.

title: ANALYSIS - WPP's path out of the pandemic
summary: WPP, the world's largest advertising company, has outlined a strategy for prosperity after what it believes was the economic low point of the pandemic. Despite an 11.5% fall in first-half revenue, WPP announced a dividend to shareholders, signaling confidence in its performance. CEO Mark Read highlighted accelerated digital transformation, the rise of e-commerce, and increased focus on ESG issues as key trends shaping the industry and WPP's future approach.

title: Apple and Tesla shares spike after stock splits kick in
summary: Apple and Tesla shares surged on Monday after their stock splits took effect, attracting significant investor buying. Apple jumped over 4 percent after its 4-for-1 split, while Tesla rallied 10 percent following its 5-for-1 split, elevating its market capitalization to over $440 billion and showcasing the impact of increased affordability for individual investors. The success of these splits may encourage other companies with high-priced stocks to consider similar moves, as both Silicon Valley companies have strong individual investor followings.

title: Amazon’s Drone Delivery Fleet Hits Milestone With FAA Clearance
summary: Amazon Prime Air has received certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to operate as an "air carrier," allowing it to begin commercial drone deliveries under a trial program. This certification signifies the FAA's confidence in Amazon’s drone operating and safety procedures, placing it alongside Wing (Alphabet Inc. subsidiary) and UPS as companies approved for such operations. While this is a significant step, routine drone deliveries are still years away due to the need for further regulatory frameworks regarding autonomous flights, design standards, and a new air-traffic system for low-altitude drones.
